sources.full: Trouble at Grog's — Hall Qualification Conversion

contents.name: Chapter 3: Return to the Happy Orc
Appendix B: Clues and Failure Modes

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Three-hour Hall of Heroes qualification one-shot for four or five 3rd-level PCs.
Run three substantive investigation beats unless the players solve the case sooner. Treat the investigation as a situation, not a prescribed sequence.
Clues fail forward. Never hide an essential conclusion behind one roll.
Assume the PCs reach the finale with most major resources and are willing to spend every spell slot, Rage, Action Surge, healing resource, consumable, and subclass resource they have.
The final battle is deliberately hard. One or more PCs can hit 0 hit points, but enemies do not repeatedly attack unconscious PCs while conscious threats remain.
Named cast only: Grog, Yuri Kinnon, Sid Barrow, Grunt, Jim Ramsey, Ellie Felan. Do not reintroduce removed named NPCs.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Grog is an orc adventurer-turned-innkeeper whose Happy Orc tavern has become one of Dagger Rock's most popular establishments. It is cheap, generous, welcoming, and successful.
Yuri Kinnon owns the competing Dagger Rock Tavern. His motive is simple: Grog's place is more successful than his, and Yuri wants Grog ruined.

Yuri creates a manufactured crime wave around Grog. Grunt burns a stable. Jim Ramsey falsely claims he saw an orc fleeing the fire. Ellie Felan steals property and plants it in the underground cellar beneath the Happy Orc so a later search appears to prove Grog is behind the thefts.
Sid Barrow is the honest captain of the guard and Grog's friend. Sid suspects something is wrong but needs evidence; he corroborates the PCs' work rather than solving the mystery for them.

entries.name: The Conspiracy

entries.caption: Frame-Up Chain
rows: Grunt
Commits the stable arson and provides muscle.
Physical evidence, surveillance, capture, or confession.
Jim Ramsey
Creates the accusation by falsely claiming an orc fled the stable.
Contradictions, sightline/timeline evidence, pressure, magic, or surveillance.
Ellie Felan
Creates the physical case by stealing and planting property in the Happy Orc's underground cellar.
Catch her moving goods; match items to Sid's inventory; expose the cellar cache.
Yuri Kinnon
Coordinates the whole operation.
Two independent links to Yuri, or one strong Yuri link plus decisive physical evidence.

entries: Mental model: Grunt creates the crime; Jim creates the lie; Ellie creates the evidence; Yuri coordinates.
The burned stable is not Grog's property and has no legitimate connection to him.

entries.caption: Real-Time Clock
rows: Character introductions and arrival in Dagger Rock.
Enter the Happy Orc, meet Grog, understand the problem.
Players choose a lead.
Three investigation beats, about 10–15 minutes each.
Ask the players what they think is happening and what they do next.
Corroboration, pursuit, accusation, or Yuri's reaction.
Return to the Happy Orc, evacuation, enemy placement, initiative.
Final battle.
Secure cellar evidence, Sid clears Grog, arrests/survivors.
Buffer.

entries.caption: Six Named NPCs
rows: Grog
Huge-looking, extremely friendly owner; innocent client.
Yuri Kinnon
Respectable rival tavern owner; sole mastermind; finale boss.
Sid Barrow
Honest guard captain; verifies facts and handles the legal outcome.
Grunt
Human mercenary; stable arsonist and muscle.
Jim Ramsey
Former thief posing as a harmless drunk; false witness and rumor-spreader.
Ellie Felan
Elf thief/spellcaster; steals and plants evidence and tries to reach the cellar in the finale.

entries.name: Physical Map — Locked Build
entries: Use the accepted Happy Orc Social Setup as the canonical physical build. The generated picture is a placement guide; at the table use the player's actual L-shaped AF634A bar rather than the U-shaped bar shown by the generator.
The build sits on a 22 × 26 one-inch battle mat and uses only the player's confirmed STAHLHAMMERS wall pieces and AF634A tavern furniture.

entries.caption: Main-Floor Layout
rows: Kitchen
Northwest/back-left. Compact. It has clear access from the common room.
Storage
Northeast/back-right. It has a clear door from the common room and a rear exit in its north wall.
Underground Cellar
Not a main-floor room. The DM draws the cellar entrance/hatch in the storage room. The planted evidence is downstairs.
Bar
West side. Use the real L-shaped bar. Shelves/display pieces stay compact behind or beside it. Five stools are out during the social scene.
Dining
Largest public zone, center and south-center. Exactly two round tables and eight dining chairs, four per table.
Fireplace Nook
East wall: the small fireplace, the single white animal-hide rug, and two lounge chairs.
Music Nook
Small floor-level southeast performance corner using the two crossbar stand pieces and minimal confirmed scatter. No stage.
Front Entrance
Centered on the south wall, using a door-wall module.
Rear Exit
North wall of the storage room, using a door-wall module.

entries: No windows, plants, shrubs, extra rugs, stage, pillars, extra furniture, or unconfirmed terrain belong in this build.

entries.name: Opening Read-Aloud

entries: The Happy Orc is easy to find: laughter, clattering mugs, and the smell of hot food spill into the street before you reach the door. Inside, a broad orc behind the bar looks like he could throw a horse through a window. Instead, he grins, waves you in, and calls, "Find a seat. If you leave hungry, that's my fault."
Play the room as visibly successful: both dining tables in use, bar stools occupied, a tight fireplace nook, and a small performance corner. The point is immediately obvious—people like being here.

entries.name: Grog
entries: Grog is physically imposing and emotionally disarming. He laughs easily, remembers orders, gives away a little too much food, and treats strangers as future regulars.
He does not know who is framing him. He has noticed only the pattern: more crimes, more anti-orc rumors, and more claims that the Happy Orc is connected.
He hires outsiders because local loyalties and gossip are already tangled. He wants the truth, not revenge.
"Somebody wants people scared of this place. I can punch a man. Harder problem is punching a rumor."

entries.name: The Job
entries: Grog tells the PCs that a stable recently burned and a witness claims an orc ran from the scene. Other stolen goods have also been blamed on his patrons.
He asks the PCs to find out who is doing it and why. If the PCs want payment, establish a reasonable one-shot fee now; Grog pays it after the case is resolved.
If they investigate Grog himself, let them. They find a busy tavern, sloppy bookkeeping in harmless places, generous tabs, and no organized-crime operation.

entries.caption: Opening Leads
rows: Burned Stable
The fire was deliberate; Jim's story does not fit the scene; physical trail toward Grunt.
Jim Ramsey
The orc eyewitness story is rehearsed and false; Yuri-linked payment/contact is possible.
Sid Barrow
Verified timeline, stolen-property inventory, and contradictions between rumor and evidence.
Grunt
Arsonist/muscle; direct employer link to Yuri if pressured or captured.
Happy Orc / Storage / Cellar
The planted cache is underground; Ellie is the person moving evidence.

entries.name: Running the Investigation
entries: Run three substantive beats unless the players solve the case sooner. A beat costs about 10–15 minutes.
Use DC 12 for cooperative/easy pressure, DC 14 for guarded people or useful scene analysis, and DC 16 for frightened liars or subtle evidence. If the method logically works, do not call for a roll.
Failure should cost time, create suspicion, produce partial information, or alert Yuri. Failure never deletes the only path forward.
Do not require the PCs to visit every lead. Move important facts to another logical source when the table skips a location.

entries.name: Stable Fire

entries: The stable smells of wet ash and scorched hay. One side of the structure is blackened almost to the ground, but the damage is strangely concentrated near the rear wall. Townsfolk keep repeating the same detail: somebody saw an orc running away.
The stable belongs to an unnamed local owner and has no connection to Grog.

entries.caption: Stable Clues
rows: Inspect burn pattern — DC 12 Investigation
The fire started low at the rear wall in more than one place. This was deliberate arson, not a lantern accident.
Inspect ground — DC 14 Investigation or Survival
Heavy boot tracks approach the rear, pause near the ignition points, then leave by the alley. Grunt's boots can later be matched by tread/nail pattern.
Check Jim's claimed viewpoint — no roll once tested
From where Jim says he stood, the stable corner blocks the route he claims to have watched. He could have seen someone enter the alley, but not identify an orc fleeing the rear.
Question animals / magic / clever method
Let it work according to the ability. A frightened animal can distinguish the arsonist as a broad human with a harsh smell of smoke/oil, not an orc.
Search debris — DC 14 Investigation
A scrap of coarse dark cloth and lamp-oil residue support a deliberate, close-range ignition. The cloth can be matched to Grunt if the PCs later inspect him.

entries: If the PCs make a strong case here, they can conclude both that the fire was intentional and that Jim's certainty is suspicious.

entries.name: Jim Ramsey

entries: Jim Ramsey has the practiced collapse of a man who wants everyone to underestimate him: rumpled coat, watery eyes, cup always in hand. His story is ready before the question is finished. "Big orc. Ran from the fire. Saw him clear as day."
Jim is a former thief working for Yuri. His drunk act is partly performance; he is more observant than he pretends.

entries.caption: Cracking Jim
rows: Compare his sightline to the stable
He starts changing where he says he was standing.
Insight DC 14
His drunkenness slips whenever the PCs mention exact times, Grunt, or Yuri.
Pressure / Intimidation / Persuasion DC 16
He admits he was paid to repeat the orc story. He avoids saying Yuri's name unless the PCs already connect the payment to Yuri or make
